utterances.text: I would interpret the role of General Mladic as follows: I believe that Belgrade has given him broad scope of authority for command and control of operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but that, ultimately, Belgrade continues to be responsible for whether or not those operations continue, and that there is some evidence that in the course of this year Belgrade has been saying to General Mladic that maybe this is time to stop the war. So, what I am suggesting, as a matter of interpretation, is that General Mladic on a day to day basis has been running the Serbian military in Bosnia, but that he does not run it without reference to instruction or opinion in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just turning back to the war itself and the nature of the war that was conducted, was there any involvement, for example, in the network of camps that were established ultimately, and Belgrade participation in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One part of the project, that this Serbian project to create a new entity involved the establishment of a network of camps in parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but Belgrade's involvement can be noted simply by the presence of some of those detained, some of the non-Serbs detained by Serbian forces who were taken to camps, to prisons, on the territory of Serbia itself. For example, at the military airforce base by Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the VJ have any involvement in the war in Bosnia itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The VJ has maintained involvement at certain stages, giving assistance to the VRS. One example would be in the early part of 1993 when Muslim forces were attacking Bratunac near the border with Serbia, VJ artillery fired from Serbian territory against the Muslim forces in support of the VRS. In the same period, forces, VJ forces, were reported crossing the border from Serbia into Eastern Bosnia and moving to the Brcko corridor towards the north west. Other examples: In April 1994, elements of the Nis and Uzice corps from the VJ were present in the attack on Gorazde. Perhaps one example of the overall co-ordination between the armed forces of these apparently separate Serbian entities, that is, the army of the republic of Serbia and Krajina, the area in Croatia, the army of the Serbian republic, that is, the VRS in Bosnia and of the VJ is a series -- is the air attack carried out in February 1994. In this case pilots who had been training at the Podgorica air base in Montenegro were transferred to the Udbina air base in Serb-held Croatia from where they flew missions on behalf of the Bosnian Serb army before four of six planes were shot down by NATO aircraft in pursuance of Security Council resolutions on an air exclusion zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the VRS continue to receive support in the form of equipment and things of that nature from either the VJ or from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is -- there have been credible reports that the VRS has continued to receive assistance from Belgrade. One clear demonstration of this is the admission himself by President Milosevic himself in an address to the Pale assembly in May 1993 in which he made clear that Belgrade had been giving assistance. Other examples include the presence of particular pieces of equipment which appear to be new and to have come from Serbia and Montenegro. One recent example, I believe, was in the news only in the last few days, or an item it was in the news in the last few days in connection with this, in the early part of this year Belgrade was involved in the transfer of new air defence systems to the Bosnian Serbs. These were later destroyed by NATO aircraft. They were then recently replaced, and I understand there were some attacks in the last few days in an attempt to remove them again after they locked on to NATO aircraft. These are some of the signs of the continuing support coming from Belgrade for the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing with the pattern of the attacks that took place in Bosnia in the spring of 1992, in your opinion, was the spring offensive of 1992 planned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my opinion, the spring events of 1992 was planned. The evidence of the Serbian preparations through the declarations of autonomous regions in the autumn of 1991, through the preparations and mobilisation of the JNA in that period and through the systematic and co-ordinated nature of the attacks in April and May 1992, I would say that this is evidence of a planned and co-ordinated attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would other features of the plan be the utilization of the paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The paramilitaries would be one essential part of the plan; the plan with the aim, I would say, of controlling territory and carrying out the act known as ethnic cleansing relied on the paramilitaries to secure control of particular areas, to instil -- to carry out particularly unpleasant acts in some cases and to instil terror as part of the process of inducing populations to leave their homes. Another part of the evidence of planning in all of this is that the bureaucratic capability of this new statelet was put in place immediately. Documentation was available, rubber stamps were available as the bureaucratic and administration process for dealing with the non-Serbian population was put into effect. This, I think, was another sign of planning and organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the establishment of the Crises Committees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed. The Crises Headquarters I mentioned earlier again are another sign of this planning shadow government being put in place some months beforehand, ready to appear and take over the administrative control of territories the moment that the declaration of the independence of the Serbian Republic in Bosnia and Herzegovina was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of the establishment of the camps themselves, would you see that as part of the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The existence of camps over a widespread part of the Serbian held territory in Bosnia, the way in which the camps were used and the way in which the camps fitted in with the administrative processes for separating non-Serbs from the Serbian populations in these areas for means of either separating and in some cases it is supposed killing, and in other cases arranging for them to be sent away from these territories, appears, quite clearly, to reflect systematic preparation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything, in particular, that you would refer to to demonstrate evidence of planning by the JNA itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The evidence of planning by the JNA, I think, can be determined from observation of events as they happened at the time, but can also be taken from the words of people in the JNA themselves. In particular, General Veljko Kadijevic, who was the last Federal Secretary of Defence and senior General in the army, who has indicated, as I think I may have mentioned this already, the project of creating a common State for the Serb people, and of the need -- and of the planning and preparation which went into this and, indeed, the JNA providing the backbone and the corps of the VRS as it carried out the project in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the fate of the territorial defence that you spoke of earlier when talking of the two tier structured of the military establishment of Yugoslavia, what happened to the territorial Defence as a consequence or following upon these attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the preparation period for the war in Bosnia, different things happened to the territorial defence system. In areas where Serbs were in a dominant position, the territorial defence system was organised for use by the JNA and by the Serbian leadership in this campaign. In other areas, the JNA either disestablished the territorial defence structures or in the process of co-operation with the Bosnian government interior ministry succeeded in disarming territorial defence structures in many parts of Bosnia. There were some parts of Bosnia, for example, Croatian communities in Herzegovina, where the local Croatian authorities managed to hold on to some of the territorial defence weaponry. This was particularly an issue in the early part -- in the period leading up to the outbreak of widespread hostilities in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the paramilitary units participate in the preparations for the spring offensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The paramilitaries were an integral part of the preparations for the offensives. They were -- I would say they were to be the shock troops leading the fight. Their mission was to assist in securing control and assist in destabilizing Bosnia. The attacks in which they were involved all focused on key communication points, in the first instance, the points of access into Bosnia and Herzegovina which would mean that the Serbian forces either controlled access in or could deny access to non-Serbian elements coming into Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then moving on to try to take control of key communications points throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, to control the movement of traffic and military equipment throughout the country as far as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned the establishment of the Crisis Headquarters, as such, were there any other sort of non-military steps taken by various groups in relation to the preparation that you know of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb leadership in one sense, as I have already indicated, was going through a series of pronouncements, declarations, arrangements of political structures for independence for the future. They also took over the administration of areas which quickly came under Serbian control, and before that in the parliament had been suggesting that if Bosnia were to become independent, then, in the words of Dr. Radovan Karadzic, the Bosnia Serb leader, it could mean the end of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any evidence of the local Serb population in Bosnia being informed in advance of what was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were reports in a number of cases that before the paramilitaries or the JNA attacked particular towns, the local Serbs were given an effective warning by the announcement within some network for the Serbs that there would be an evacuation drill. This meant that the Serbs themselves were not present in the towns often at the times when attacks occurred. I cannot say that this means that no Serb was present in the town, but that very often large numbers of Serbs were taken outside the town. I believe this happened in places such as Prijedor, Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to an attack upon a particular area, was there any agitation or provocation prior to the commencement of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was often what might be described as an act of provocation immediately prior to the introduction of either JNA or paramilitary forces into a town. One example could be a grenade thrown through the window of a Serbian shopkeeper. This was taken as a pretext for the JNA or for the Serbian paramilitaries or both who had been waiting outside the town immediately to step in to impose order, to have discussions with local non-Serbian leaders, often to arrest them, certainly to reach initial agreements on the arrangements for political control within that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of the other side of the conflict; were preparations made by the non-Serbian community in Bosnia in relation to these impending attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some limited preparation by the non-Serbian communities. I indicated a little while ago that the Croatian communities, or some parts of the Croatian communities, in Herzegovina held some of the weaponry of the territorial defence system when the JNA was trying to disarm it; that other elements were present armed from Croatia, the Croatian paramilitary groups; that there were to be some elements of the Croatian army present in Bosnia. The Bosnian government, having complied to a large extent in the process of disarmament of the territorial defence force, was left in a weak position. That weak position did not mean it had no armament but that it had very little armament and, in addition, it could look to some small Muslim paramilitary groups, but these were small and pitched against the capability that the Serbs would have in what was to be the VRS was insignificant. So, you were looking at a situation in which, although there were elements in the Croat and Muslim communities which had some armament, in essence, they were in a very weak position vis-a-vis the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to the beginning of hostilities, or the beginning of hostilities themselves, could you describe for the benefit of the Chamber what the Serbian forces did to the opposition and, particularly, to the non-Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The attacks tended to include many similar features in each place. We mentioned already the acts of provocation prior to an attack. Once an attacks had taken place, there would be segregation of the non-Serbian communities. Segregation would take place by gender, by age and in many cases by what, for want of a better term, I may describe as intellectual capability. In this process, men of military age and particularly those capable of some kind of leadership were taken separately from women, children and elderly people. In many cases, those intellectuals who might form a political leadership were killed. In other cases, all the men of military age were taken to a particular detention camp. At the same time, women, children and the elderly might be taken to detention camps or they might begin the process of expulsion from where they were. The process of expulsion would involve administrative procedures in which the individuals in question would be asked to sign a document in which they would transfer their property and other rights to the local Serbian authorities. They would then be asked to pay for or offered the opportunity to leave which would require them to pay for a one way exit visa and one way ticket to be transported out of Serbian controlled areas. This process of separation and segregation resulted in communities which were predominantly Serb in all these areas. It resulted in the killing of people in a number of cases. In other cases, the pressure and the processing through this administrative procedure to remove them from the territory which the Serbians wanted to control. That territory -- this programme, integral to the idea of ethnic nicks cleansing and involving the camps which we mentioned earlier, was a mechanism by which through killing or through intimidation the Serbs would secure complete control of the territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any particular features common to the tactics used to induce terror into the community, I mean the non-Serbian community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The process by which this took place had common features. Within towns it could involve, after the segregation, it could involve the demonstrative killing of certain individuals to send a Mesic to the rest of the population. A common feature could also be bombardment from surrounding forces, particularly by elements from the JNA, later the VRS, and it involved in the case of -- in many cases, particularly in those taken to camps, acts which would generally be considered to be of extreme violence. Apart from those places where people would be -- those places where people could be killed, there were numerous places where there was extensive beating and also many reports of areas where there was mass rape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the process employed to seize political control in the various towns that were taken by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The process of establishing political control began with the secret establishment of the Crisis Headquarters I mentioned before. The Crisis Headquarters were usually established in conjunction with the States Security Services, that is, Serbian State Security Services. These shadow governments waiting to take over were pronounced at the moment a takeover occurred. When that happened, the Serbian leaders in the Crisis Headquarters then began to take over local control. They removed non-Serbs from significant positions within the political community. They restricted the movement of non-Serbs. In some cases only Serbs with particular -- only non-Serbs with particular types of work to carry out were allowed permits to enable them to move within the area and movement for them was strictly controlled. The mechanism for controlling movement was the mixture of the issue of permits to allow movement, and a series of check points established in towns and within the areas of the Opstinas generally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any evidence of attacks upon non-Serbian cultural or religious symbols?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the common features of the attacks was that non-Serbian property could be destroyed. In the case of individual properties, in some places such as, I believe, Bosanski Novi, this could involve the identification of non-Serbian households through the marking by the hanging of a white sheet from a window, and then these houses would then be destroyed. In other cases, key items of religious or cultural significance such as Roman Catholic churches for the Croats or mosques for the Muslims would be deliberately destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have touched upon, I think, the purpose for which the camps were established. How widespread were these camps that were established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camps were widespread. They were throughout the areas of Northern and Eastern Bosnia under Bosnian-Serb control, and throughout this territory appeared to share many common -- appeared to be part of the same systematic network.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at this document I am about to show you? (Handed) What does this document represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document shows the locations where it was reported in 1992 that the Bosnian Serbs had established camps of the type we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was prepared on the basis of information provided by the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the United Nations Security Council, and I believe in this form was prepared on the basis of the United Nations Security Council documentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place the document upon the video machine, and could you take us through the document pointing to the various places that you see there? By all means approach the machine to point to aspects of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You will see, as you look across the map, that all the way from the very north western part of the country through northern Bosnia and down through eastern Bosnia into the south, close to the border with Montenegro, were the locations in which these camps were reported to have been established. Some of the most significant ones, those most well known, were in north western Bosnia, in particular, the camps at Prijedor, Omarska, Trnopolje and Sanski Most, but, as you see, there was an extensive network of camps in other places, including for the purposes, I believe, of the case you were looking at now, Vlasenica in Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wherever there is a name appearing in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina on that plan, you say that that represents a camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the exception of the name of the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina at Sarajevo, I would say that the names -- the information on this map for the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina shows where it was reported that camps were established within the territories under Serbian control in 1992. I believe it does not indicate all the places that were reported to the Security Council by the Bosnian government, and that these are areas in which it is -- that it is believed that there is reasonable evidence to believe that camps existed in those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to move on to a new area now. Does your Honour wish to have the adjournment now or would you prefer me to continue with the questioning?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Thank you very much. I think that, well, now it is 20 to 4, so, firstly, could I suggest that either you or the witness could tell us how much longer this testimony might last? If we are talking about a testimony which would last, let us say, another 15 to 20 minutes, then I would propose that Dr. Gow complete his testimony and then following the break, the pause, we would begin the hearing of the witnesses, eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think it is possible, your Honour, that we could finish in 15 minutes, 15 to 20 minutes, so I will continue. (To the witness): Dr. Gow, in relation to your report that you prepared initially for submission to Her Honour Odio Benito in relation to the confirming of the indictment, did you also include in that some reference specifically to the Opstina of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did. In preparing the document for the use of the Office of the Prosecutor, I carried out some work specifically on that area. That information was put into this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just in relation to that Opstina at the period of, say, the beginning of 1991, from your researches, firstly, can you tell us the main industry that was carried out in the region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe the main industry in the region concerned mineral resources and mining, particularly the production and processing of bauxite and aluminium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what the population of the Opstina of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, I believe the population was a little over 33,000, of which about 7.5000 were within the town of Vlasenica itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In percentage terms, what was the largest ethnic group in the Opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe the single largest group within the Opstina was the Muslims and, as far as I recall, they constituted something a little over 40 per cent of the population -- nearly 42 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your researches, were you able to establish who held most of the leading positions in the town in terms of ethnicity prior to the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appears that most of the leading positions in the town prior to the war were held by members of the Muslim community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Vlasenica part of an area declared to be part of the Serbian autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlasenica was explicitly part of an area declared to be within the Serbian autonomous region of Bihac which was declared, not at the time of the others in September 1991, but in January 1992. However, I would say that the status of this autonomous region is a little bit uncertain. At some stages it is referred to -- it was referred to as the Serbian autonomous region of Romanija-Birac. Romanija was one of the areas declared in September. At other times, it is referred to as the Serbian autonomous region of Bihac. Whichever at whatever stage, it seems fairly -- it is clear that it was part of one of the areas declared as Serbian autonomous region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Vlasenica attacked as part of these attacks by the Serbian forces that you mentioned earlier in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlasenica was attacked as part of the Serbian project in April 1992. I believe the attack came at the end of April, on the 30th, and it shared, as we pointed out before, some of the features common to the attacks in all the other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned also in your evidence, when you were talkin generally of patterns, that often there was a provocation before the attack occurred. Were you aware, from your researches, of any provocation specifically that took place prior to the attack here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not able to recall the specific acts of provocation in this case. I do recall that there were acts of provocation and, if you wanted, I could proceed to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. From your researches, did the JNA become involved in these attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is clear that the JNA was involved in the attack on Vlasenica and in taking control of the area. There are reports of the presence of elements of the JNA Novi Sad corps. Novi Sad is the town within Serbia itself, in the province of Vojvodina. The elements of Novi Sad corps were present at the time of the attack and as the takeover was taking place and, indeed, that they continued to be in the area after the 22nd May, at which point the JNA was supposed formally to have divided, that is, these units from the Belgrade military continued to be in the area after the time at which the non-Bosnian Serbs were supposed to have withdrawn and departed the VJ on the territory of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What military hardware did the JNA use in the attack on Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The equipment used involved primarily armoured personnel carriers and heavy machine guns. There was also some use of mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were local Serbs mobilised at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Local Serbs had been mobilised in preparation and, as the takeover was taking place, I believe more of the local Serbs were inducted into the Serbian -- into the local Serbian territorial forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of the JNA, were any mobilised into the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, as I indicated some time ago, in this process of mobilisation, some Serbs in local communities would be mobilised into the territorial defence forces and others would be mobilised into the JNA reserve, and in this case I think both happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your enquiries, what happened to the non-Serbs who held government posts in Vlasenica following the occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Following the occupation, the non-Serbs in significant political positions were removed from their positions; the reports that some were killed, some were taken to a particular point of detention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were restrictions placed upon the movement of non-Serbs in this Opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Consistent with the pattern of activity I think I identified a short time ago, in the Vlasenica case as well restrictions were imposed on the movement of non-Serbs. The non-Serbs were either -- in many cases were dismissed from their jobs if they held senior positions. Some of those who were allowed to continue working could only work if they could move. They could only move if they had a special permit because they were allowed because of the special employment -- because of the special nature of their employment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the paramilitary groups that you spoke of earlier in your evidence play any role, so far as you were able to discover, in relation to the attack upon Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some reports of the presence of paramilitary groups in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the name of those groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I no longer recall the names of the groups, but I do believe that the groups of -- I have a -- I think I recall that the group led by Zeljko Raznjatovic (Arkan), "The Tigers", was in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also from your enquiries, were you able to establish whether or not a camp of the sort that you described in your evidence earlier established in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was -- a camp of the type I was describing was established and it was named, and the name was given to it was Susica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would your Honour excuse me a moment? Those are the questions that I wish to direct to this witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Judge Odio Benito would like to ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Was there a tradition of tolerance between the different religious groups in the former republic of Yugoslavia? Perhaps closely related with this, how did the people of the different republics get along before 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer to a question of that kind, I suspect, to be comprehensive would have to be very extensive and very long. If you permit me, I will try to give a brief answer to it which I recognise is likely to be a little incomplete. The relationships between the different religious and ethnic groups in the SFRY, I think, to a large extent depends on area. For the most part, relationships between the different groups were harmonious. There is reason to suppose that in some parts of Croatia those areas particularly in which there was intense fighting and in which there was massacre of Serbs in the Second World War, that they continued after the -- under Tito's Yugoslavia there continued to be some difficulties, some ethnic tensions in those areas. I find it very hard to say more than that without having been in this place through all that time and experienced it myself. I am aware also that in the province of Kosovo, which I recall I mentioned earlier in the day, with the majority of Albanians in the area but with some Serbs, and with the idea that if it had been a very important place within Serbian culture, they were quite clearly tensions within the community there between the Serbs and the Albanians. For the most part in the rest of Yugoslavia, it would seem to me fair to say that there was a reasonable degree of tolerance in relationships between the differing communities, but that this probably has to be -- in saying this, you probably have to think that what is general has to be pitched against considerations in particular areas and in particular local communities. In the case of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it has often been said that Bosnia could be recognised as a place in which there was great harmony between the different groups, and I think that it is fair to say that for most parts of Bosnia, particularly for the main urban areas. I would add, though, that I am aware that there was some parts of Bosnia, particularly in the course of the 1970s and 80s, as there were processes of migration from Serbia into Serbian both by Muslims and by Serbs, that people with a slightly different perspective were changing the balance in some areas. I can say no more than that. It would be very hard to construe any firm conclusion from that, but I do think it is the kind of thing which is worth noting if you want to try to understand and try to get a feel for this question of the tolerance between the peoples. There was a considerable degree of tolerance. It was probably never quite the brotherhood and unity in most places that Tito and the communists wanted it to be, but that a lot of the time people were able without much problem to get on with each other and to work side by side where they needed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO-BENITO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Gow, I gathered at various times in your testimony that there was an undissimulated military participation of Serbian and Montenegro forces in the conflict; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, would you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an undissimulated participation of the military forces of Serbia in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An un?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Undisputed, I mean, it was clear. One of the forces you mentioned, there was -- I quote your words -- a planned and co-ordinated attack in spring 1992. Co-ordinated by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The plan, in my judgment, was planned and co-ordinated by elements in the JNA and by elements in the Serbian Security Services and in the Federal Security Services of by then the former SFRY. I believe in testimony I mentioned that, in my interpretation, the Deputy Federal Interior Minister in the SFRY, Mihail Kertes, and the Head of the Serbian Security Services, Radmilo Bogdanovic, were implicated in the organisation of these forces, and that elements within the JNA were also involved in organising the paramilitaries and in planning and carrying out the series of attacks. We should note that at the time we are talking about the attacks that it was elements of the JNA which were present in Bosnia, and that were involved in the actions taking place as they had been in Croatia before that, but that in the case of Bosnia it was quite clearly elements of JNA acting under command from Belgrade which were involved in the initial phase of the war in April and May 1992 until Belgrade, in face of the prospects of UN Security Council action, decided to carry out this action by which they divided the JNA into the army of the Serbian republic in Bosnia and the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that after the date Bosnia was recognised as a State?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was -- Bosnia was generally recognised as having independent, international personality on 7th April 1992, and it was on 22nd May 1992 that the Belgrade decided to divide the JNA into the army of the Serbian republic in Bosnia and the army of Yugoslavia. So, therefore, it was after the date on which Bosnia was generally recognised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a State?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a State.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At another instance you mentioned that there were some kind of detention camps in Serbia for Bosnians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it for military people or for civilians? The detention camps were in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camps to which I referred ---

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- were on the territory of Serbia in Sremska Mitrovica and at Batajnica. As far as I recall, the camps included military personnel. Without checking, I would hesitate to be certain that they involved civilians but I believe they might have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they treated as war prisoners or what was their status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Their status, as far as I can see, their status was not clearly defined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] I would like to ask you whether you know whether the concept of ethnic cleansing is to be found somewhere, either officially or less official, in documents or proclamations as organised plans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The term ethnic cleansing has been widely used. It does have some history, but it has come to prominence and has been used in a widespread way in connection with the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina and, particularly, with the Serbian campaign there. The term is often attributed to one of the Serbian paramilitary leaders, Vojislav Seselj, in the current context. It has also been used by one of the other Serbian paramilitary leaders, Zeljko Raznjatovic (Arkan), and there is some film evidence, I believe, in which Arkan is giving instructions to his troops to be careful in this particular cleansing operation. But to say that there is some official document in which a plan for ethnic cleansing appears, I think, would be to take -- would be to make too strong a statement. I have seen no evidence of an official document in which the term "ethnic cleansing" is used, but the term has been used and it has been used by some of the people involved n the activity that they have been carrying out.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] No. In that case, the court would like to thank Dr. Gow for your complete, compact and detailed testimony. I think you have finished for the moment, Mr. Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Perhaps one could accompany the witness before we adjourn because I would like the witness to be taken out before we discuss a further point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] We are going to resume, if you do not mind, at 4.20. We will have a 15 minute break, and I would like to ask you right now whether the first witness will do as we have already arranged, namely, the possibility to disclose his identity, name, address and elements of identification, but he must be informed of his rights that he will be concealed from the cameras. We would like to know how we should call him when he gives his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases, I had put in train a process where I was to be informed if the witness had changed his mind in relation to giving evidence in public. I have not received any messages so I can only assume that is the case, but during the course of the adjournment I will check again. If there is any alteration in that position, I will have a Mesic brought to your Honour to that effect. I just might say, however, your Honour, that I would, irrespective of the position of the witness, request that the address of the witness not be revealed in the course of evidence in any event.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] That is what you have agreed with the first witness you are going to call upon?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. With respect to the question of the address, I would ask that none of the witnesses' addresses be given in public. I certainly will not ask the witness to give his or her address and I would ask that not be asked of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] We can go along with that completely. So we will meet back here in 15 minutes. (Short Adjournment) 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] You have the floor, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, in relation to the next witness that we wish to call, this witness has informed me during the break that he wishes to give his evidence in public. We would, therefore, request that the order of non-disclosure that applies in relation to this witness, and in so for as it applies to this witness, that it be lifted. Your Honour, it is our understanding that the addresses of the witnesses would not ordinarily be given, and certainly it would not be the intention of myself or the Prosecution to ask the witness the address, but if there is any ambiguity about it I would ask that the order for non-disclosure remain in force in so far as it would apply to the address of the witness. Subject to that, I would ask that it be lifted in relation to this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Could you specify for which witnesses, because now we can name them?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I can specify the name of the witness that I would now seek to call, that witness being Munib Ahmetovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] I look at my colleagues to see if they agree, Judge Riad. We will partially lift and I ask the Registrar to take note that we will lift the order of non-disclosure partially as regards the identification elements, except for the address, and generally speaking to meet the request of the Prosecutor formulated just before the pause, all eyewitnesses which will have until the 18th October we agree that the minimum degree of protection will be the address which will remain private. Therefore, we will take note of this change and amendment and, if you like, we can now ask the witness Munib Ahmetovic that he takes the oath and then answers the questions that you put to him relating to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If it pleases, your Honour. MUNIB AHMETOVIC, Sworn.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Do you hear me? Can you hear the translation, the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Original in Bosnian] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Can you hear the translation from French into your language? Could you please remain standing to read the oath which I believe you have before you. We are listening to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Original in Bosnian] I solemnly declare that I shall speak the truth, the only truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Please be seated, sir. Please sit down. Before the Prosecutor puts his questions to you which will be the general guideline, I would like to tell you that the court is aware of the conditions under which you wish to testify. It was stated that you have been completely informed of the rights which are granted to you for your own protection. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, and I think also on behalf of the Prosecutor and the Registrar, I would like to tell you that you are here within the legal framework, and that what the Tribunal wants above everything else is that you can relate your testimony as serenely as possible with the knowledge that you are going to be protected by the Tribunal. I would also like to inform you that the Tribunal and all the legal participants are fully aware of all you have done to try to come here in The Hague, far away from your home, to relate to us what you have seen, suffered and often heard. Before starting, I would like to tell you if at any point of time whatsoever you have difficulties, regardless of its nature, do not hesitate to inform us. Mr. Prosecutor, you now have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As your Honour pleases. Your name is Munib Ahmetovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in Skugrici, the Opstina of Vlasenica, Bosnia Herzegovina, on 12th August 1960.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live from the time of your birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the region of Opstina Vlasenica, except for the five years of my education, schooling, and 13 months of working in the Opstina of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your work in the Opstina of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Opstina of Vlasenica I was a religious official or worker. I was an Imam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you for the benefit their Honours give a short explanation of the role that was performed by an Imam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An Imam is a person who works in a given area, which might be several housing communities, local communities. He is the leader, a religious leader, of all the citizens who feel as believers in that area. I was that kind of official in Vlasenica, in the town of Vlasenica, which included also several villages, which covered several villages; some 20 hamlets and small villages were also part of my area and they belong under my Jamut, "Jamut" meaning the community of religious people, congregation of faithful. I was working in Vlasenica from 1st February 1983.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the religion is the religion of Islam; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you might expand just a little for their Honours on where the Imam fits in the hierarchy of religious people that work in the religion of Islam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An Imam is a person who is in direct contact with people, with the believers, with the faithful people. He has full authority in working with people in his area. He has a person above him that is the chief or main Imam, so there are several Imams sort of reporting to a main or chief Imam. Above this there is a republican level, the hierarchy goes up, and this is called the Supreme body, the Supreme Court for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Then there is the Riasset which is still higher, where the main leader of the Islam community is Raes Illuema, that is his title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vlasenica did you work in the mosque in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you may have mentioned earlier, but did you receive special training to become an Imam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in order to become an Imam one had at least to complete secondary religious school, secondary denominational school, which is the Gazi (indecipherable) Madresa in Sarajevo. At the time when I was at that school it lasted for five years, the education lasted for five years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would, I would ask you to cast your mind back to 21st April of 1992. Were you then at that stage in the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was, I was in the town of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about 7 a.m. on that morning of that date of 21st April 1992, can you remember what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I woke up around 7 o'clock that morning. I know very well it was a Tuesday on 21st April 1992. As I was waking up I felt, I heard rather detonations or explosions. At first I thought that I was dreaming, but then I got up and I went to the toilet and as I was washing in the bathroom I heard explosions very loudly because my bathroom window was open, and I realised at that moment that Vlasenica was being occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you home alone or were you with members of your family at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I was alone. My family was in my native village of Skugrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard these detonations going on, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I decided to leave the town, because my car was parked in front of my house. At 7.30 precisely I walked towards employ car. Entering the car, or as I approached the car, there was nobody in the street, at least I did not see anybody, and approaching the car I first came with my keys, I tried to open the door, unlock the door, but as I was unlocking the door somebody said, "You by the car there, enter the car and sit down", and I did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that moment where the voice came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not quite sure, but I assumed that it must have come from a neighbouring house or building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did as told, I entered it, my vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For some 20 minutes I remained in the car and then I tried to get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you tried to get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I heard a voice again which told me: "I told you to go into the car", it was a very sharp voice, "If I don't hit you, if I don't not shoot at you there will be somebody else shooting from the other building." So I raised my head and I looked round and saw, on neighbouring buildings I saw armed people in camouflage uniforms. So I came back to my car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment did you recognise the uniform that the people were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the camouflage uniforms were of the kind worn by the former army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the former army", what army are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am referring to the army of the Yugoslav National Army, the JNA, which I had served myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you got back into the car. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 15 minutes later a car, a police car, came along with three persons in that car, and they stopped near my car. They asked me who I was. When I told them I was an Imam they said that they were actually looking for me and they invited me to come in their own car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you armed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a pistol for which I also had a permit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the people that invited you to get into the police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I entered their car they asked me whether I was armed. I said, yes, I had a pistol, and they took it away from me. Then I entered their car. Then they asked me, they told me they were commanders of the Serbian Special Guards and that they are now disarming the Muslims. They told me that since I was the Imam, that I was a respectable a person, and they asked me that I should invite all the Muslims to hand in their weapons. At that moment I told them that that was counter to my vocation and my knowledge and on my position as an Imam, but after that they very crudely and sharply said: "You must do it or you won't be there any more." I saw that I had no chance, stood no chance of resisting, so I accepted what they asked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could just tell us again, what was it precisely they wanted you to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They actually wanted me as an Imam to invite the Muslims of Vlasenica to return or hand in their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I agreed to do this we started driving through the town. They invited people, then they asked me to invite people as well, to repeat their words, to speak them, to speak these words, but also first identify myself to say, "This is your Imam speaking, Munib Ahmetovic".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said these words, did you say it just with your natural voice or was your voice amplified in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My voice was amplified. They had a megaphone, the car megaphone, police car megaphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were travelling around Vlasenica, did you see any armed Muslims in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see any and I am sure there were no such people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any deadlines set in order for people to surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember very well that the first deadline was 9.15 in the morning, 9.15, for the handing in of the weapons at specified points: in front of the department store, in front of the police station and in the hospital, local hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the first deadline, was that later extended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They extended it until 11 o'clock roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Mesic that you gave to the Muslim people of Vlasenica, were you required to say anything about the position of the Serbian people in the town, in other words, were you asked to make any statements about the position of the army or the position of the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Were you told to tell the people that the town had been surrounded by the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I might tell you the kinds of words which they asked me and forced me to utter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me that I should say the words which they had first said, roughly like along the following lines: "This is Munib Ahmetovic speaking, your Imam speaking. Vlasenica is surrounded. The authority has been taken over by the Serbian Special Guards and we ask you to come to the collection points in front of the department store, the police station and the hospital to hand in your weapons until or before the particular deadline 9.15 or 11 o'clock later. Unless you do this we will destroy the city or the town. We guarantee or the Serbian Special Guards guarantee to you use all complete security if you hand in your weapons." That roughly was the Mesic which I was asked to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you were aware, was that order to the Muslim people complied with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where the Serbian headquarters were in Vlasenica at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that. As they were driving me through the car, because I was in their car all the time except for short times that I was allowed outside the car, they were the commanders of the forces occupying Vlasenica, so they came to their headquarters which was at the Panorama Hotel. They also entered the police station, the local police station, building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. While you were driving around in the car, did you overhear any conversation that was going on between the Serbian policemen that were driving you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard what they were saying to each other. They were giving some orders, or they were saying things are proceeding satisfactorily or not proceeding or something like that. At one point I felt, it was later, I actually felt that they were satisfied that what has been achieved is exactly what they wanted. You could see it in their faces. Also they mentioned the names of the more respectable people, citizens of Vlasenica, so they say: "This is the house of Fadil Turkovic" who until that time had been the local police commander in Vlasenica, and they pointed out some other buildings. Then you could feel that they were sort of expecting some people to return. Fadil Turkovic, the former police commander, they asked him to come back to Vlasenica. They had some contact with him but he did not return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Turkovic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak of prominent citizens of Vlasenica, to what particular ethnic group are you making reference, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were only looking for Muslim citizens, Muslim respectable or respectable Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier in your evidence that the forces that were the JNA forces that were in the town and you recognised the uniform, did you happen to know what Corps the JNA forces were that were involved in the military exercises in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know it at that time, but later I spoke to many Muslim citizens of Vlasenica who had been in contact with the soldiers with whom they drank coffee sometimes, and they told me that these soldiers told them they later that they were part of the Novi Sad Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to what you told the Muslim people when you were speaking to them, were you also told to tell the Muslim people to gather at a particular point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the end of that mission, around 10 o'clock, they started calling up the citizens to come to the square in front of the Civic Hall House of Culture, and they said one of the commanders would address them and that I would address them as their Imam. This exactly happened, at o'clock there was such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You attended at that place at 11 o'clock, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people had gathered at that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 100 roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first to speak was one of the military commanders. He addressed these people, telling them that they are the Serbian Special Guards, that they have taken over all rule in Vlasenica, that they have occupied Vlasenica, and that they had taken the weapons from the Muslims and that they guaranteed security for all citizens of Vlasenica, so that nobody should fear anything or that no one had any reason to flee Vlasenica. They asked me to say the same thing more or less in the same terms, so that I should confirm what they were saying and that is what happened. I actually spoke the words which they had spoken, so I simply repeated those words, which was very difficult for me and hard for me to do because I knew this was not true. I knew that Vlasenica had no security and people had no security. I saw the Muslim police having been disarmed, that in all functions and all services there were only Serbs now, no Muslims, and that in this situation the Muslims citizens cannot hope to have any security. But I had to say what they asked me to say and what they had said. But I added my own sentence which was like this, I said: "Citizens of Vlasenica, residents of Vlasenica, authorities come and go, one another, the third one, but people remain and people will always have to live here regardless of what happens. So you be patient, try to be patient, try to go through this period." In my speech, which was very brief (I spoke for five to 10 minutes perhaps), I had two applauses, heard applause at two points, but it was very painful for me because I knew what I was saying was not true. The applause showed that the Muslims had not expected what was happening, and they were sort of happy. Regardless of the changed of authority they felt, well, this is new authority and they applauded saying that they will continue to live and respect this authority, which was not their authority, which was not democratic, which was an oppressive one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the members of the Serbian forces that were there, did you recognise any local Serbian people who were members of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I recognised Goran Viskovic, nicknamed Vjetar, who was in the same camouflage uniforms as the forces that had occupied Vlasenica. I also saw Danilo Jokic while many were camouflaged, disguised with paints over their face, black, red, blue, green. There may have been other people I knew but I did not recognise them because of the painting, but I did recognise those two. I also saw, not in the same uniforms but in the uniform of the Reserve Force of the Former Yugoslav Army, I saw several individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe in a little more detail for the benefit of the Chamber the type of camouflage that the men had on their faces and how it appeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were painted with different colours and changed the appearance of their faces completely. There was black colour, green, blue, so you could see only their eyes, everything was painted, everything else was painted over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But apart from that they were then also dressed in military uniform, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They had camouflage uniforms, fatigues, worn by soldiers, the same uniforms they wear today, to this day. They are predominantly green, but various other colours too; the type of uniform which is adapted to different seasons and especially to the environment of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you described a moment earlier I think as the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people from the specialised units had said that they had taken over various strategic points in the town of Vlasenica. Did you feel that that was true from what you were able to observe at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that it was true, because driving around the town, and I covered the whole town, I saw in front of all important institutions, such as the municipality building, the police building, the hospital, the Hall of Culture, the big companies and enterprises, I saw peoples in uniform, people in uniform, in the same uniform armed with weapons standing there as security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were driving around in the car did you see any shooting take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them shooting, members of those units were shooting, and when they saw that I had seen it the people in the car who with me, who were driving me around, said that it was the Muslims who were doing the shooting which was definitely not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any armed Muslims at all in the area while you were travelling around in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. There were no armed Muslims except the ones which were handing over their weapons, mostly just rifles and pistols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean after 11 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to a Bosnian cafe. I met my colleague there, Mr. Bego Selimovic, who had spent the previous night in the apartment of his cousin and was not able to leave until 10 o'clock because his cousin was working in the bakery and had left before 5 a.m., and since the bakery had been occupied too, his cousin knowing that he was in the flat had sent him, had sent a Serb to open the apartment for him otherwise he could not have gotten out. Therefore, he was prevented from surrendering the pistol which he had a permit for. So he asked me to go with him to the police station so he could hand over the pistol for which he had a permit which is what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we went to our houses?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you hand in the weapons after you had agreed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not. They returned the pistol to me and they did not take his at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that the pistol that you had possession of you gave to the Serbian police; they kept it for a while and then gave it back to you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the same with the pistol of your friend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after this you went back to your home, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not take away his pistol on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. After this what did you do? Did you then go home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we went to our houses for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a certain time aware of the situation in which we were, tried to get in contact with some friends of mine, Muslims. I tried to ring them, many of them. I could not reach them, probably because of the situation, because I myself could not move around much. So I telephoned Redjo Hatunic who was a teacher in the secondary school solely to exchange opinions with him, what to do in such a situation. I greeted him with the Islamic greeting of "Selam". The response was also the same, in very good pronunciation, "Selam", from the person at the other end of the line. I asked if it was Redjo. The response was that this is the Commander of the Special Serbian Guard. Then he added: "You see Ofendija" which is a title of honour, "how well I can say this." I looked for Redjo and he let me speak to Redjo. I asked Redjo how he was. In an excited voice he spoke to me, saying: "What shall I tell you? What can I tell you? You see, they are searching my house. They are looking for weapons and I don't have any." Then he hung up. About two hours after that I again called the same number to try to reach Redjo Hatunic because I was curious what was going on with him. His wife took my call, Nila Hatunic is her name, who told me that he had been taken away. I have never seen him since, and Nila Hatunic, Redjo Hatunic's wife, in 1993 when I went to the Tuzla region where I saw Nila Hatunic I found out from her that Redjo had never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What then happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That evening we did not dare spend the night in our flats, so we spent the night with our neighbours, Ismed and Amin Gobalic, and this is how the day was spent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The day after that we did not have the courage to go to our flats, or we did so very rarely, but still in the afternoon we went to our flat. Of the several Muslim young men in the street in front of the house, these young men told us that eight men in camouflage uniforms, those who had occupied Vlasenica, had been walking around our flat. It was clear to us they were looking for us. So we went into the flat, took some of the basic necessities and then went to a neighbouring flat, the one occupied by Fikret Dautovic where we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you then do after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We made a firm decision to try to leave Vlasenica, but in the beginning we did not know how to. Early in the morning my colleague Bego Selimovic came to the idea for us to call by telephone our colleague the Serbian priest Milorad Golijanin and ask his help, ask for his help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the Serbian priest of Vlasenica, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The priest of what religion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian religion, orthodox Serbian, orthodox priest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly at 7 o'clock Bego, my colleague, telephoned the orthodox priest Milorad Golijanin and told him our wish, about our wish. He said: "I know what you need. Wait for me, I will be there in half an hour."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly at 7.30 the Serbian priest was in front of our flat. I invited him for coffee which he said "No" to, saying that it was not time to drink coffee and that we should immediately go to take care of what we need to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get the impression from what he said to you and his appearance that he was prepared to help you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So we went to the former Bauxite company, Bauxite mining company, administrative building, and we heard from people we met there that this was the crisis headquarters for the Opstina of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There we met Milenko Stanic who until that time, until the occupation, before the occupation, had been the mayor of Opstina of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Milenko Stanic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We met here also another Stanic, I think his first name was Slobodan, who was in the uniform of the Reserve Forces of the Former Yugoslav Army. I know that his rank was that of a captain and, according to information which I learned later, he was the commander of the Reserve Troops which remained in Vlasenica following the withdrawal of the shock troops which had occupied that town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was uniformed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it was the crisis headquarters in Vlasenica. Why did you go to that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that building, that was the Bauxite company administrative building, this was the town which had actually been abandoned just before the occupation of Vlasenica, because the Bauxite company was a company which was the largest and economically most solvent company in Opstina of Vlasenica. So just before the occupation of Vlasenica they had left this administrative building knowing that it would be -- they went moved to Milici, that is another village, leaving this building for the occupying headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to this place, did the Serbian priest say anything to the people that appeared to be in charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me just say before that, that in addition to two Stanics there was also Danilo Jokic who was in a special uniform. So the Serbian priest addressed those present with a request. He said: "Well, you know, we know that you have special passes allowing people to leave the town. You know these people that I am bringing, which means myself and my colleague. Don't let anything happen to him and, if possible, give them the passes so they can leave the town. I know that they feel uncomfortable in this situation, so please help them." These were the words of the priest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the Serbian officials then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two Stanics were very nonchalant, very jovial. They said there is no need, why would we need the passes, we are not in confinement, we can move freely, that is what they said, but Danilo Jokic spoke in very ugly terms and he was very rude to the Serbian priest, saying there was no need for us, he said: "Why are you advocating their cause? If they need something they should come on their own." However, nobody gave us any pass and they actually notified the priest that the passes were issued by the police station and not by them. They also said that the chief of the police station had been replaced or rather the head of the department of the interior of the city, Rade Bjelanovic, was changed and there was a new name Mane Dzuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after this, after you had been told this, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we left the building and the Serbian priest and my colleague Bego left in his car, and I was in my car and we moved to the interior department of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the interior department of the city", is that often referred to as the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we used to call it SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the police station we met the new head of SUP, Mane Dzuric, who had a briefcase, and I remember this very well. The Serbian priest approached him and said: "You know these people", because he knew us of course. "We are coming to you" said the Serbian priest "to ask whether you can help." He took us to his office in which the story was the same as in the crisis headquarters. The Serbian priest again asked for the passes for the two of us, and at one point the former head of the SUP, Rade Bjelanovic, also came. So both Rade Bjelanovic and Mane Dzuric were both Serbs. So the previous head of the interior and the second was Serbs. But again they did not give us the passes. They said, "You don't need that".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We left the office, but in the ante room to that office the Serbian priest was called back then; he was told to go back to the main office. So we waited for him and when he came for the second time, when he emerged, we noticed a great change in his face. As we were leaving the building, walking towards our cars, he told us: "These are the bandits, there is a gang of people," those that he had visited. "I am afraid even for myself, even I don't feel secure any more." So we came to our cars and then he said: "If you wish to go towards Kladanj I will take you in my car and I take that responsibility." He and my colleague Bego Selimovic actually sat in his car, that was Yugo brand. I sat in my car. So they moved, they drove off towards Kladanj and I drove towards my house or my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The colleague that you referred to, Selimovic Bego, was he also an Imam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Bego Selimovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bjelanovic is a Serb. Bjelanovic is a Serb and Mane Dzuric are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is my pronunciation that has confused. Bego Selimovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bego Selimovic is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You call him your colleague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is my colleague.
