utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, was he like you also an Imam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I interrupted what you were saying, but you said that you got into the car after the Serbian priest had offered to take you to Kladanj. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I would not go to Kladanj because my family was in Skugrici. So the two of them sat in the Serb priest's car, so my colleague Bego Selimovic and the Serb priest sat in the Serb priest's car and they headed towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I headed towards my house, or rather my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came in front of my building I saw in the rear view mirror of my car, I saw another car, that same car which on the first day the police used to drive me round the city, that car now overtook me and stopped in front of me, and the three persons, three men, the three commanders as they called themselves, they came and my colleague Bego Selimovic actually came out of that car, emerged out of the car, because they had been stopped at the first checkpoint outside Vlasenica and they were returned. So I came out of my car and we went to my apartment. They took our guns, my pistols, my pistol and my colleague's pistol, and they searched my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they took us to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to the police station what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the police station were these three people, these three commanders of the Special Guards, and there was another person there in the same uniform, in the same camouflage uniform. Then there was also myself and my colleague, plus two people who were in civilian clothes and who were local Serbs. They were Zoran Pantic for whom I know that he was married, I knew that he had been married to a Muslim woman, Maria Masmilovic, and there was a second person Ljuban Stanisic of whom I know that he used to work as an administrative clerk in SUP issuing identification cards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the police station what did they then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They put before us empty sheets of paper, blank sheets of paper, and said: "These are the papers that you should use to write everything that you know about the weapons owned by Muslims, about the main Muslim people, who they are, where they are and so on."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was in particular that gave you this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that paper was handed to me and to my colleague also by one of these three commanders, those from the car who all the time spoke about himself, referred to himself as a commander of the Serbian Special Guards. He had long hair down to his shoulders and if I could see him today I would recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write anything on the paper that you were given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first, no. After a couple of minutes when they saw we were not writing at all, they took away my colleague Bego Selimovic, they said: "Now we'll separate you", and then I never saw Bego Selimovic again until 1994 when I came to the liberated territory. I remained alone in that room. For a long time I did not write anything. I was looking, staring at this paper, saying to myself: I don't know anything, I won't write anything. However, they told me that I know things, that I am one of the main organisers of resistance, that they have all the data about me, alleged data. I denied everything. I said, "All of this is not true, I have nothing. I don't know anything. There is no resistance" I told them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seeing that I am not writing anything, at one point they brought in Zoran Surkovic who comes from a mixed marriage and was my friend. They asked him to say that he had acquired weapons from me, a gun, which of course he denied because it was not true. The person who had given us this paper then hit him several times with a heavy military soldier's boot into his chest. The man was actually seated in a chair. He was a very strong and well-built man, but he was hit so hard that he fell from the chair. I told that man that he had not taken anything from me, he confirmed this and was taken away to another part of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that kicked Zoran Surkovic in the chest in the way you have described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was hit by the commander of the Serbs Special Guards, the person who presented himself as a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again seeing I was not writing anything, that I was not admitting anything, that same person, the same commander, hit me four to five times, saying: "We know everything, and you do not want to admit this or confess." At that moment he was so angry he just left the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he hit you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He hit me with his fist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the head, on the face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened as a result of him hitting you in the face? Did you remain standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was seated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Did you stay in the chair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in a standing position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he struck you, could you describe what force he appeared to apply when he hit you in the face with his fist, in terms of was it a full blow or a half blow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think that these were full blows because I would not have remained in the chair, so he did hit me but not very strongly, not very powerfully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What then followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left the room, as I have said. He brought in immediately, after a very short while, only a minute or two, he brought into the same office, into the same room, he brought Mevludin Hasanbegovic, a Muslim from Vlasenica, who had been to prison. He could not have been brought from the town because his house was about 10 to 15 minutes distance from SUP. On his face one could see that he had been maltreated, that he had been beaten, and he was asked to say that I was with him, working with him to arm the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, yes, Munib helped me to arm the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that true or untrue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of Mevludin, did you know of him to be involved in supplying of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I knew nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seeing that I have no way out of this situation because it went on for quite a while, they tried to speak nicely to me again. At one point they said that I had helped them the first day, so that Muslims in the villages, that means outside this town proper, had not handed over their weapons, so if I confessed it would be made possible for me to go to these villages because they would follow your advice. At that point I felt that there was a possibility for me to leave the town with a firm decision not to come back, but I was also aware of the fact that I have to confess something, so I started writing my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you confess to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that statement I confessed that I had armed Muslims allegedly, supposedly, and I also said, which was true, that I was a member of the Democratic Action Party, the Muslim Party, which I was. Basically I lied everything else in my statement, except the fact that I was a member of the Muslim Party in the leadership, local leadership. To be convincing I gave quite a large amount of weapons and I think they believed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you had given this statement did they appear to be satisfied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These three, in fact now four of them, the three that had been in the car that presented themselves as commanders and the fourth one in the camouflage uniform, had walked out of the office while I and Stanisic went to another office where a clerk typed my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time for your Honour to adjourn or would your Honour wish to continue with this witness until the conclusion of his evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Well, I think it is up to you whether this is a good moment to stop and whether it is a relevant moment to stop. I think you should also ask the witness whether he is tired. Usually we finish at 5.30 each day. Could you perhaps continue a little more today and, if possible, we could perhaps continue a bit more, if you can agree with that. So, firstly, are you not too tired? Do you feel all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Original in Bosnian] As far as I am concerned there are no problems. I could go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will continue with the witness, your Honour. After the statement had been typed, what happened then? What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While the statement was being typed we were sitting. At one point during the typing of the statement Stanisic told me that I had money and that I was obliged to hand it over. I pretended not to hear his sentence, this sentence of his, but 10 minutes after that I asked them if I could go to the toilet. They allowed me to. I went to the toilet for one reason only; I wanted to take the money that I had in my shirt pocket, about 5,000 German marks which was my own money, take it out of the pocket and put it in one of my socks, which is what I did. I went back to the office, and when my statement was completed Stanisic picked up a piece of paper and said: "We will give you as a receipt that you have handed over your money." I said: "I had no money on my person." He asked me where the money was. I said the money was in the mosque and it was not my money, because I was also the treasurer of the Islamic community of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say to you when you said that the money was in the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said: "Let's believe you. Go and get the money".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got up and went towards the mosque. I walked rather slowly because at that moment I was not quite sure that I was not being followed. When I came to the gate of the mosque I saw standing by the window of my house Miss Zineta Dautovic, a woman who had seen me being taken to the SUP, to the police station, and also the woman in whose apartment I had spent the night, the previous night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went into her apartment, her house, I even had coffee with her. I did so for a reason, for a good reason, just to make sure if I was being followed. I went out, having told her prior to that time that I would try to flee, escape, either I could escape or I would be killed, but it was not my intention to stay on in the town. I told her to tell her husband Fikret and everybody else that she can get in touch to leave the town of Vlasenica, because at that moment I was completely convinced that the safety of Muslims that they had supposedly guaranteed would not really be, that there would be no safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left the house and just went through the movement of walking into the office of the Muslim Islamic community, I did not take anything out of the office, and then went back to my car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the car near the car I saw Aida Ferhatbegovic. I also told her what my intention was. I got into the car and started driving towards the bus station, taking the shortest possible route. The road to the bus station goes around the town. Going for the police station from the SUP towards the mosque, I saw along the road a police patrol in blue uniforms worn by the police prior to the occupation. I recognised among them a policeman, a former policeman, whose name is Milan Govedarica. From that fact I concluded that there were police there. That is why I took the short cut. When I came to the bus station and was about to come out to the main road between Vlasenica and Kladanj I had thought of two ways out of the area, two roads: One was to lead from the bus station to the right, as far as the petrol station, this is the road to Milici; the other was to the left towards Bijelo Polje or the Alpro factory. The second possibility was to come out at the bus station to the main road, to the main Vlasenica Kladanj road, left towards Kladanj, after about 50 metres right towards the main road. Then in the Muslim graveyard, from that Muslim graveyard head towards Darakovic. Both of these roads were free from the police at the time, and those two points were usually, they were police at those two points usually. Exactly at 14 hours I left Vlasenica. I decided on the road towards Milici, the one that went to the right, which seemed shorter and in fact was shorter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Having arrived at the petrol station, I saw many soldiers dressed in this special uniform, but the petrol station is not exactly on the edge of the road; it is about 20 metres, maybe fewer than that, from the road. I went off the main road and headed towards the Alpro factory to the left. At the Alpro factory, just before the factory, the road branches off in two directions: One direction leads to Toplik, a Muslim village, the other towards the factory itself. On the road to the factory I saw an armed soldier who was wearing the uniform of the Reserve Forces, a local man, that is a local man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But he was not standing by the road that I had taken. So I went on my way towards Toplik, and that way I got out of the town. In that location between those two roads I saw an armoured vehicle. I was not quite sure whether it was a tank or an armoured vehicle transporter. I had seen seven such vehicles on my first day when I was taken around the town in that car. At the very entrance to Toplik I caught up with Ibrahim Berbic whom I knew quite well. I told him about my intention and told him to tell that to my congregation, and then having come out of occupied Vlasenica, of the occupied part of Vlasenica, went on my way to my native village. I was able to cross that road only because that day, 23rd April, was extremely hot. It is a dirt road and there is part of the road that had only just been cut which is hardly a road to speak of. On that part of the road fortunately I had no problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached your native village, is it true that it had not been occupied by the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, that was not occupied by the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then remain in a village not far from your native village called Cerska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came to my native village Skugrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then subsequently did you remain in that village until Cerska was occupied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it was occupied did you move to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your wife and children evacuated by UNPROFOR in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in March 1993 my wife and my children went over to the region of Tuzla, to the free area of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of 1993 did you go to Kladanj on foot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kladanj I went to Lukavac because my wife and children were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions of the witness, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] I think that we have finished the testimonial?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: [Original in French] Thank you very much. The court thanks you very much for your testimony. We will resume tomorrow at 10 o'clock. (The proceedings adjourned)
